rv.q: The songs have gone unmentioned so far for a reason – they're the weakest thing here, which is a problem in a musical.
And, just in case I have left you in any doubt, Flyby is one of the best new British musicals I’ve seen in years, bold in conception and execution and dazzlingly performed.
It’s undoubtedly a perplexing piece, and while the book could do with a considerable amount of revision, it is deserving of admiration for being so unusual and wilfully uncommercial.
These sections add less, and indeed it is the show’s space-escape premise that proves its biggest challenge.

What he is given to say is verbose, and the show often seems to be going around in circles rather than moving forward. None of this is Thompson's fault: he is as believable as the writing allows him to be and, luckily, achieves tremendous pace in much of what he does, almost convincing us that what he has to say is actually worth saying!

Stuart Thompson, as Daniel, is brilliant in bringing the character to life, portraying a whole range of emotions. The same can be said of Gilbert who gives a meaningful performance. Gina Beck, Rupert Young and Simbi Akande are also excellent throughout.
While the fabric of the show is flawed and flimsy, the production looks great. Lenson’s direction is precise, with clever details sprinkled throughout.
Flyby reaches for the stars, yet without a clear trajectory it drifts, and it is only the exceptional cast that stop this journey into the void from feeling entirely weightless.
